chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) was in Kufa, riding the mule of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Then he passed by the fish market and said: 'Do not eat and do not sell from the fish that does not have a shell/skin.'

key_terms.بَغْلَةَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The mule of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for fish to be considered halal according to Imam Ali in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) direct judicial authority in Kufa, where he utilized the Prophet’s mule as a symbol of his inherited leadership while addressing market regulations. By specifying that fish must possess a 'qishr' (shell or skin) to be permissible, he established a foundational criterion in Shia fiqh that distinguishes edible fish from other sea creatures, emphasizing both ritual purity and commercial fairness in public markets.
